paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: fear and trust can show up in the same breath, and David lets them. He says, "When I am afraid, I put my trust in You." (Psalm 56:3) He doesn't wait until the fear is gone. He doesn't fake being brave either. He takes the fear straight to God, and I think that's the whole recipe.

And look what David leans on. He says, "In God, whose word I praise—in God I trust. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?" (Psalm 56:4) He says it again in verses 10 and 11, like a man pressing a stamp twice to make the lines come out clear. Trust isn't a feeling that falls on you like flour from the top shelf. It's something you say, on purpose, about the God whose word you praise.

Then there's the tender part, and it gets me every time. David says, "Put my tears in Your bottle—are they not in Your book?" (Psalm 56:8) So your hard days are not lost on God, baker. He has delivered David's soul from death and his feet from stumbling, "that I may walk before God in the light of life." (Psalm 56:13) So next time the fear comes knocking, tell God about it, trust Him out loud, and walk on.
